summary: This is a sound stage-1 rewrite aimed at the largest gap on the board: pooler m=128 is 25.7 us against a 14.6 floor, and unpooler is 20.4 against 14.6. Master has not made it moot, because every landed gate is at m<=32 or on the router. Two things must change before it goes out as a scored submit. First, the reduce tail as written is self-contradictory, and the literal reading is a race. Second, none of the 9 tests reaches m 65..128, so a prepare() self-check with a cuBLAS fallback is needed.
justification: The mechanism is plausible. The parent's own diagnostics (d34fd76f9c444728.log) show wgmma emitted, 140-154 regs, no spills, and a warm no-reduce mainloop of 26.0 us on both layers, or 2.6 TB/s. Its judged kernels ran 28.2 us (pooler) and 25.6 us (unpooler), against today's nvjet at 25.7 and 20.4 us (FINDINGS verify_16 rows). Both layers move the same 67 MB and have the same per-CTA work (128x2048 weight slice, 512 KB), and their mainloop times are identical. That points to a shared per-CTA streaming limit, which wider 256 B TMA rows and producer/consumer overlap target directly. The rewrite is not just the m<=16 TMA result again (LESSONS: TMA added little there), because m=128 runs at ~128 FLOP per weight byte and the loads have to leave the MMA warps' issue slots. The expected directions match TASK.md: verify_16 pooler/unpooler should be faster and everything else flat, since the 65..128 gate is disjoint from master's m<=16, unpooler n==1024 and 17..32 swap-AB gates, and m=130/256/512/1000 stay cuBLAS. Each row has weight 62 inside one load of five shapes, so a ~6 us pooler gain is worth roughly +1.5-2% on the geomean. The weakest link is the milestone yardstick. M1/M2 are stated in prepare() event times, but the parent's warm event 'full' figure (32.55 us) was above its cold-L2 judged kernel time (28.2 us), so those numbers carry ~3-4 us of event/launch overhead. Judge M1-M3 on profile top_kernels, and use the prepare prints only as a mainloop-vs-tail ratio. On design, the floor at BLOCK_M=BLOCK_N=128 is not just DRAM. Every CTA also re-reads its x K-slice from L2 (pooler: 512 KB x per 512 KB of weight), so L2-to-SM traffic is ~2x the weight bytes. That may cap this tiling above ~1.5x of the floor, and it argues for the stage-2 BLOCK_N 256 or multicast idea. It does not block stage 1, whose target is <=24 / <=19.5 us.
confounders: sglang-gemm-dispatch-parity: only as the incumbent. The new path replaces its _bf16_gemm_dispatch_impl call at pooler/unpooler m=128 and nowhere else, so this is not a confounder, just the comparison baseline.

bf16-shape-gated-triton-winners-combo, bf16-m32-swapab-wgmma-triton: disjoint gates (m<=16 / unpooler n==1024 / 17..32), their own workspaces and counters, and cold L2 per replay. No shared launch, memory traffic or numerical path at m=128, so no interaction. The only coupling is code: the spec says 'Built on master (658d63b)', but master is 8b9ad43, so it must be built on 8b9ad43 and must not disturb the swap-AB gate.
router-triton-hilo-fused-control-splitk-all-m, router-hilo-at-m8: different layer, untouched. No confound.
interference: No companions. No landed hypothesis touches pooler or unpooler at m=128, so ab-revert or ab-tune would measure nothing new. This is a rewrite stage judged on the replaced kernels' own time, and the prepare() prints (variant compiled, regs, PTX counts of wgmma and cp.async.bulk.tensor, mainloop vs REDUCE=False) already attribute the result to TMA/warp specialization or to the tail. Splitting the three bundled mainloop changes into controls would spend checks the next stage needs. The in-flight bf16-cublaslt-algo-pick-in-prepare-m128-m256 overlaps on these two rows by a different mechanism; per-shape rows decide which one a combo keeps.
rules_flags: Correctness hazard, not a rule break, but critical on a scored submit. The spec says the CTA drawing the last ticket 'does NOT store' its partial. In this ticket scheme every CTA stores before it increments, and it can only learn it is last after incrementing. Taking the ticket first and storing only if not last would let the winner read a sibling's partial before it is written, which gives wrong output on timed calls. Keep store-before-ticket for every CTA: the winner skips only reloading its own slice (adding acc from registers). Only the 64 KB reload comes off the critical path, not the store. Tickets first plus per-slot ready flags and spinning would need all 128 CTAs co-resident (1 CTA/SM at 192 KB smem on 132 SMs). Do not do that.

Test coverage: none of the 9 pre-timing tests falls in 65 <= m <= 128 (m=130 unpooler stays cuBLAS), so the first check of this kernel is the timed-call correctness check of a scored run. Add a prepare()-time self-check per layer at m in {65, 96, 128} on synthetic x: rel L2 vs torch.matmul fp32 < 1e-3, a single-nonzero-row exactness probe, and the ticket counters back to 0 after two back-to-back launches. On failure, fix a state flag in prepare() that routes the layer to cuBLAS. The flag depends on weights and synthetic data only, so it is allowed.

Compile resources: 3 stages x (32 KB x + 32 KB w) = 192 KB smem, plus warp-specialization barriers and any layout-conversion scratch for the 128x128 fp32 epilogue, can exceed 227 KB. Catch OutOfResources in prepare() (master already imports it for swap-AB) and step down to num_stages 2, then fall back to cuBLAS. Print the variant.

Allowed as written: the TMA descriptor is built from the weight in prepare(). kernel_fn gates on cfg layer/m/n/k and x dtype/contiguity only. Prints stay in prepare(). The fp32 sum order varies with the winning CTA, which is non-deterministic but far inside 1%, and single-nonzero rows stay exact because the other partials are zero. Workspaces and counters are allocated in prepare(). No host syncs.
open_questions: Does Triton 3.8's tl.range(warp_specialize=True) accept a loop that mixes a TMA descriptor load (weight) with a masked pointer tl.load (x) on sm90? If it only compiles the plain variant, the run measures TMA plus BLOCK_K 128 alone, and the printed variant must be read before judging M1. Consider a host TensorDescriptor for x built per call in kernel_fn (no caching; OOB rows zero-filled, which removes the mask). Check that it captures correctly in the CUDA graph.

Is the 26 us mainloop limited by DRAM issue or by L2-to-SM traffic from re-reading x (~2x the weight bytes at BLOCK_N=128)? If M1 stalls near ~20 us even with warp specialization compiled, stage 2 should take BLOCK_N 256 (one x read per 256 weight rows) before stream-K.
Masked rows at 65..127 are never scored and never tested. Is it worth warming and self-checking them, or should the gate be m == 128 only, to shrink the untested surface on a scored run?
